name: Allocate costs to clients and bill them
function: finance (financial planning, cost allocation and client billing)
summary: The manager charges its clients only what it costs to run, so each quarter finance allocates actual operating costs to pools, segregated accounts and client portfolios with agreed keys such as assets by strategy and team time, adds external manager fees, custody and deal costs that belong to specific accounts, and issues each client portfolio a cost allocation statement and invoice. The work waits for the corporate ledger close and for external managers' quarterly fee invoices, runs in a spreadsheet model that must allocate every dollar with nothing left over, and passes director, committee and CFO review. Client finance staff scrutinise the statements against budget and query keys, the fourth-quarter statement waits for the audited true-up, and the case ends when the client pays.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian provincial not-for-profit asset manager recovering about $217 million of its own operating costs a year (2021) plus agency external fees from four public-sector clients with five portfolios, with a four-person planning and cost allocation team using an ERP and spreadsheets.
baseline.notes: 2021 recovery of costs revenue of $216.6 million and total costs of $473.7 million including external fees (mgr_ar21).

unit_of_work: one client portfolio's quarterly cost allocation statement
trigger: Quarter end, with work starting when the corporate ledger is closed for the quarter.
end_state: The approved statement and invoice have been issued, the charges are posted to the client's portfolios and pools, and the client's payment has been applied.

volume.seasonality: Five statements each quarter, issued in the first month after quarter end; fourth-quarter statements wait for the audited annual true-up in late February or March.

evidence.note: Clients are charged their share of the model manager costs on a cost recovery basis (mgr_ar21, pclient_ar21); five portfolios in 2021 per the organisation file. Quarterly invoicing follows the organisation file's assumption, since the model manager does not publish its billing frequency.

steps.name: Wait for the quarter-end corporate ledger close
steps.description: The cost allocation analyst waits until corporate accounting closes the model manager's own ledger for the quarter: payroll and incentive accruals, vendor invoices, data and technology costs and premises costs posted, and the trial balance released.
outputs: confirmation the quarter's costs are final

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Corporate close of eight to ten business days after quarter end is an author estimate for a 240-person organisation; payroll and accounts payable feed the ledger per the process map.

steps.name: Extract actual costs by cost centre and tie to the trial balance
steps.description: The analyst exports the quarter's operating costs by cost centre and expense type from the ERP into the allocation workbook and ties the totals to the trial balance, separating compensation, IT and data, professional fees, premises and other costs. The extract serves all five statements, so per-statement time is a share.

error.defect_description: A cost centre mapped to the wrong cost pool.

evidence.note: The model manager's operating cost categories: compensation and benefits, IT and data, professional fees, pension and other supporting costs (mgr_ar21). Times are author estimates.

steps.name: Update the allocation drivers
steps.description: The analyst updates the keys: average assets by pool and segregated strategy for each client portfolio from the month-end accounting packages, team time-allocation percentages by strategy, trade counts by account and the number of private holdings, and checks each against the prior quarter.

error.defect_description: Average assets taken for the wrong months or a new pool left out.

evidence.note: Costs are allocated to the model manager products, segregated assets and clients under a cost allocation policy (mgr_ar20); pooled costs are shared in proportion to ownership (bci_pooled); a peer names assets under management and each client's asset mix as the main cost drivers (bci_car22). Time and activity keys are author assumptions.

steps.name: Chase managers for missing time-allocation returns
steps.description: The analyst emails department heads whose teams have not returned the quarterly estimate of time spent by strategy and asset class, and uses last quarter's split if nothing arrives by the cut-off.

error.defect_description: Stale split used for a team whose work shifted.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Run the allocation model
steps.description: The analyst runs the spreadsheet model: shared operating costs are spread first to investment strategies and support functions, then to pools and segregated accounts by assets and activity keys, then to each client portfolio by its holdings, and the client's share by cost category is produced.
outputs: allocated operating costs by client portfolio

error.defect_description: Formula range misses a new pool column.

evidence.note: The model manager allocates and recovers all operational costs from clients under agreed cost allocation principles (mgr_ar21) and its policy (mgr_ar20); a peer recovers all expenses through its pools and segregated client accounts (bci_car22). The spreadsheet model and stage order are author assumptions.

steps.name: Assign directly attributable investment costs
steps.description: The analyst adds costs that belong to specific accounts: external manager fees validated by fund accounting, custody fees and deal-related legal and due diligence costs, each charged to the pool or segregated account that incurred it and so to its owners.
outputs: direct investment costs by client portfolio

error.defect_description: Manager fee charged to the wrong client's segregated account.

evidence.note: External management fees, custodial fees and other investment costs are paid by the model manager as agent and recovered from clients (mgr_ar21, pclient_ar21); a public pension custody contract allows asset servicing invoices up to 60 days after period end (nmerb_ps). The wait is an author estimate.

steps.name: Reconcile allocated totals to the ledger and monthly accruals
steps.description: The analyst checks that the total allocated to all clients equals total costs in the ledger with nothing left over, and compares each client's quarterly total with the three monthly accruals already booked in its portfolios and pools.

error.defect_description: Rounding difference accepted that hides a missing cost.

control.basis: Cost recovery principle in the client agreements: all costs allocated and recovered, without profit

next.condition: fully allocated and close to accruals

evidence.note: Full cost recovery without profit (mgr_ar21, client_manager). Difference rate is an author estimate.

steps.name: Investigate and correct the allocation difference
steps.description: The analyst traces the difference to a mapping error, a missing driver, a late journal or a formula break, corrects the workbook and reruns the model.

error.defect_description: Fix applied to one client's tab only.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Explain variances to budget and the prior quarter
steps.description: The analyst compares each client's costs with its share of the approved annual budget and with the prior quarter, in dollars and basis points of assets, and drafts explanations for the main movements such as new hires, technology projects or a change in asset mix toward private markets.

error.defect_description: Explanation does not match the allocated figures.

evidence.note: Actual costs are monitored against budget and reported to clients (mgr_ar20); clients measure the model manager costs in basis points against targets (pclient_ar21).

steps.name: Director reviews the allocation and explanations
steps.description: The director of financial planning reviews the allocation results, key movements and variance explanations, compares each client's share with the budget forecast shared with clients, and approves or sends back for correction.

error.defect_description: Error missed in review.

control.basis: Preparer and reviewer separation for cost allocation under the model manager's cost allocation policy and guidelines

evidence.note: Policies for cost allocation with appropriate controls and tiered approval authorities (mgr_ar20); fee calculation and billing is an area asset managers may include in SOC 1 scope (sifma_soc1). Rework share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Decide whether allocation keys or methods changed
steps.description: The director checks whether this quarter introduces a new key, a change in method or a material shift in allocation, such as a new pool launch or a new client, which needs committee approval and advance explanation to clients.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Pool launches in 2020 to 2022 changed what was allocated to pools versus segregated accounts; share is an author estimate.

steps.name: Cost Allocation Committee approves the change
steps.description: The Cost Allocation Committee, chaired by the CFO, reviews the proposed change with its effect on each client and confirms it is consistent with the cost allocation policy before it is used in statements.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: The model manager cost allocation policy and guidelines: Cost Allocation Committee ensures allocation is consistent with the policy

evidence.note: The model manager's Cost Allocation Committee ensures cost allocation is consistent with the policy (mgr_ar20). CFO as chair, meeting wait and revision share are author assumptions.

steps.name: Check whether a year-end true-up is due
steps.description: For the fourth quarter the analyst flags that the statement must include the annual true-up of the year's charges to the model manager's audited costs; other quarters go straight to statement preparation.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: The year-end true-up to audited costs is stated in the process map; one quarter in four.

steps.name: Compute the annual true-up to audited costs
steps.description: After the external auditor signs off the model manager's financial statements, the analyst compares the year's charges to each client with its share of audited costs, including deferred recoveries for capital assets, and calculates the true-up amount.

error.defect_description: Deferred recovery of capital costs double counted.

control.basis: Client agreements: annual charges trued up to the model manager's audited financial statements

evidence.note: The model manager's 2021 statements were authorised on 24 February 2022, about eight weeks after year end, and amounts collected in advance are held as deferred recovery of costs (mgr_ar21).

steps.name: Prepare the cost allocation statement and invoice
steps.description: The analyst produces the client's statement: operating costs by category, investment costs by pool and account, allocation keys and their values, year to date against budget, any true-up, and the invoice with HST, using the standard template.

error.defect_description: HST applied to an amount that is an agency reimbursement.

control.basis: Excise Tax Act (Canada): HST charged on the cost recovery invoice

evidence.note: Cost recoveries due from clients are stated plus HST (mgr_ar21). Statement content follows the process map; time is an author estimate.

steps.name: CFO approves statements and invoices
steps.description: The chief financial officer reviews the summary of all clients' charges, the variance explanations and any true-up, and approves the statements and invoices for issue under the delegation of authority.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: The model manager delegation of authority: tiered approval of client charges

evidence.note: Tiered approval authorities in the model manager's cost governance framework (mgr_ar20). Wait and change share are author estimates.

steps.name: Relationship manager previews the statement with the client
steps.description: The relationship manager walks the client's finance or investment lead through the main changes before the invoice arrives, especially a rise in costs, a key change or a true-up, so there are no surprises at the client's committee.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: The process map notes clients' finance staff review allocations closely; preview practice is an author assumption.

steps.name: Issue the statement and invoice and record the receivable
steps.description: The analyst sends the statement and invoice to the client's accounts payable and finance contacts and records the receivable and cost recovery revenue in the ERP.

error.defect_description: Invoice sent to an outdated contact.

evidence.note: Cost recoveries are recorded as revenue and receivables due from clients (mgr_ar21).

steps.name: Post the quarter's cost recovery charges to portfolios and pools
steps.description: A fund accountant books the final quarterly charges in each client portfolio's and pool's accounts, reversing the three monthly accruals, so that pool unit prices and net-of-cost returns reflect actual costs.

error.defect_description: Charge posted to the wrong pool.

evidence.note: Pool expenses are recovered through the unit value so each owner bears its share (bci_pooled); net returns deduct investment management costs (gips_ao 22.A.24), so charges must be in the accounts before returns are final. Time is an author estimate.

steps.name: Client finance reviews the statement
steps.description: The client's finance staff check the charges against the budget the model manager shared, their own accruals and prior quarters, and either approve the invoice for payment or send questions on allocation keys or particular costs.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Clients monitor the model manager costs against targets (pclient_ar21); review time and query rate are author estimates.

steps.name: Answer the client's queries on allocations
steps.description: The analyst, with the director for policy questions, prepares backup for the queried items, such as the key values or invoices behind a cost, and replies; occasionally the review finds an error and a corrected statement or credit note is needed.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Wait for the client's payment
steps.description: The approved invoice goes through the client's own payables run and approval; payment arrives by electronic transfer or as an authorised deduction under the agreement.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Year-end receivables from clients were $36.6 million against $216.6 million of 2021 cost recoveries, about two months of charges (mgr_ar21); payment timing is an author estimate.

steps.name: Apply the payment and clear the receivable
steps.description: A corporate accountant matches the payment to the invoice in the ERP, clears the receivable and flags any short payment to the cost allocation team.

error.defect_description: Payment applied to the wrong invoice.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Chase a short or late payment
steps.description: The analyst contacts the client's payables team about the shortfall or delay, usually a disputed line or an internal approval delay at the client, and agrees when the balance will be paid.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

exceptions.name: Missing time-allocation returns
exceptions.description: Department heads have not returned their teams' time split by strategy, so the analyst chases and falls back on last quarter's split.

exceptions.name: Allocation does not reconcile
exceptions.description: Allocated totals differ from the ledger or from the monthly accruals; the analyst finds the cause and reruns the model.

exceptions.name: Allocation key or method change
exceptions.description: A pool launch, new client or new key needs Cost Allocation Committee approval before statements go out.

exceptions.name: Fourth-quarter audited true-up
exceptions.description: The year-end statement waits for the audited financial statements and includes the true-up of the year's charges.

exceptions.name: Client queries on the statement
exceptions.description: Client finance staff question keys or costs; the team provides backup and occasionally reissues a corrected statement.

exceptions.name: Short or late payment
exceptions.description: The client pays late or short over a disputed line, and finance chases the balance.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from quarter end to payment applied
benchmarks.population: Author estimate for a cost-recovery public asset manager invoicing quarterly

evidence.note: Year-end receivables of $36.6 million equal about 62 days of 2021 cost recoveries of $216.6 million (mgr_ar21), consistent with statements issued three to five weeks after quarter end and paid within about a month; p90 reflects the fourth-quarter wait for audited statements, authorised about eight weeks after year end.

benchmarks.population: The model manager statement of operations
The model manager financial statements, related party note
The model manager total costs including external fees

benchmarks.unit: basis points of the client's average net assets and CAD

evidence.note: The model manager management fees are the pension client's share of the model manager operating expenses charged back on a cost recovery basis.

pain_points.description: The allocation runs in a large spreadsheet with several stages and keys; new pools and clients break formulas and every rerun repeats the reconciliation.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the model manager launched four pools in 2020 to 2021 and moved to new systems in 2022 (mgr_ar21, mgr_ar22), each change altering the allocation structure.

pain_points.description: Time-allocation keys depend on department heads' estimates, which arrive late and are hard for clients to verify.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Clients pay every dollar and compare their share with targets and peers, so statements draw detailed queries and key changes need careful advance explanation.

evidence.note: The pension client measures the model manager costs against a 50 basis point target; the model manager reports cost metrics to clients and its Finance and Audit Committee.

pain_points.description: External manager fees arrive quarterly in arrears from many managers, and the year-end statement waits about two months for the audited true-up.

evidence.note: Agency fees collected from clients but not yet billed by vendors ($9.2 million at end 2021) and statements authorised 24 February 2022.

assumptions: The organisation file assumes monthly allocation and quarterly invoicing with a year-end true-up; the model manager publishes only that it allocates and recovers all costs under agreed principles. The year-end receivable (about 62 days of recoveries) is consistent with either quarterly or monthly invoicing.
The case covers one client portfolio's quarterly statement. Batch work done once for all five statements (ledger extract, driver update, model run) is shown at a fifth of its total time per case.
Monthly accruals for the first two months of each quarter are booked outside this case; the third month's accrual is replaced by the final quarterly allocation at s19.
Client payments are listed in triggered_by to match the process map, but in this file they close the case (s22) rather than start it; their shares are kept small.
The Cost Allocation Committee is named in the model manager's 2020 annual report; the CFO as chair, its meeting frequency and the share of quarters needing its approval are author assumptions.
The fourth-quarter statement is held for the audited true-up, which lengthens one case in four by about five weeks; some cost-recovery managers instead issue the true-up as a separate statement.

Loaded hourly costs are from the organisation file. Stated FTE (0.63) is above the hands-on time implied by 1.67 statements a month because the team also books monthly accruals, forecasts and answers ad hoc cost questions.

sources.title: The model manager 2020 Annual Report
sources.supports: New client reporting suite in 2020 with a core set of concise reports for all clients; quarterly performance recaps, positioning and commentary; KPI framework; a consistent core team for client management teams and investment committees; cost allocation policy and guidelines for fair, consistent allocation to the model manager products, segregated assets and clients, overseen by a Cost Allocation Committee; tiered approval authorities; costs reported regularly to senior management, the Finance and Audit Committee and clients; returns net of all costs, time-weighted, based on daily calculations; total benchmark daily weighted by clients' investment in each strategy; 2020 total costs $384.3 million (55.3 cents per $100).

sources.title: The model manager 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: Clean SOC 1 Type I report on the design of controls as at 30 September 2021, with Type II planned for 2022; Board and client reporting redesigned in 2021 including a Quarterly Risk Insights report; full cost recovery without profit; the model manager allocates to and recovers all operational costs from clients based on agreed cost allocation principles; 2021 total costs $473.7 million (63.1 cents per $100 of AUM), investment management costs $317.2 million, operating expenses $156.5 million; recovery of costs revenue $216.6 million; year-end receivable from clients for cost recoveries $36.6 million plus HST (2020: $17.7 million); external fees paid as agent and collected from clients; amounts collected in advance held as deferred recovery of costs; financial statements authorised by the Board on 24 February 2022; CEM benchmarking of costs.

sources.title: The model manager 2022 Annual Report
sources.supports: Inaugural SOC 1 Type 2 report with a clean opinion that controls were designed and operated effectively from 1 October 2021 to 30 September 2022; returns net of all costs using the time-weighted rate of return; benchmark policy under which Risk researches and reviews benchmarks, the Management Investment Committee recommends them and the Board approves them; net value added defined against the IPS benchmark; interim private markets administration software and a new risk and total portfolio system implemented in 2022.

sources.title: The pension client 2021 Annual Report
sources.supports: The model manager manages Plan assets for a fee based on cost recovery and regularly reports on investment performance and risk to the pension client; an Investment Management Agreement, a Service Level Agreement setting the content and frequency of reporting and service levels, and an Implementation and Support Agreement covering budgeting and cost management; the pension client monitoring program; the model manager management fees of $97.7 million in 2021 representing the pension client's share of the model manager operating expenses charged back on a cost recovery basis, with external fees paid by the model manager on the pension client's behalf and reimbursed; the model manager costs 41 basis points against a target of 50 or lower; the Board and its committees met 37 times in 2021.

sources.title: The model manager (The pension client investments page)
sources.supports: The model manager is the pension client's sole investment manager under an Investment Management Agreement, regularly reports on investment performance and risk management, the pension client runs an ongoing program to monitor the model manager's investment performance, and the model manager operates on a cost-recovery basis only.

sources.title: Asset Manager's Guide to SOC 1 (June 2017)
sources.publisher: SIFMA Asset Management Group and Grant Thornton
sources.supports: Baseline asset manager SOC 1 scope including reconciliation and client reporting; baseline control objective that account statements reflect the correct holdings and market value and are provided to clients in a complete and timely manner; reconciliation objective that discrepancies are researched and resolved timely; account performance listed as not baseline and fee calculation and billing as another area to consider; IT general controls over job scheduling, logical access and change management.

sources.title: 2020 GIPS Standards for Asset Owners
sources.supports: Time-weighted returns required for total funds; valuation at least monthly, at month end and on large cash flows; monthly returns geometrically linked; private market investments valued and returns calculated at least quarterly; when preliminary or estimated values are used the difference to the final value must be assessed and adjusted when the final value arrives (22.A.18); net-of-fees returns deduct transaction costs, external fees and investment management costs (22.A.24); material errors must be corrected and corrected reports given to the oversight body (21.A.16); benchmarks must reflect the mandate; reports to oversight bodies updated within 12 months of each annual period end.

sources.title: Custody Bank RFP, Appendix F: Performance Standards and Related Key Performance Indicators
sources.supports: Month-end close targets: 5th business day for externally managed and cash accounts, 10th for internally managed and commingled funds, 15th for alternative investment accounts; external manager position reconciliations typically received on business days 3 to 5; variances above 10 basis points of NAV explained; performance reporting due 5 business days after the month-end close; a performance revision above 5 basis points from custodian error counts as a failure; asset servicing invoices within 60 days of period end.

sources.title: Pooled funds (BCI web page)
sources.supports: Expenses of pooled funds are recovered through a reduction in unit value so costs are shared in proportion to ownership (a client owning 5% of a pool pays 5% of its costs); unit price is market value divided by units outstanding; EY performs the SOC 1 audit and KPMG audits the corporation and the pools.

sources.title: BCI 2021-2022 Corporate Annual Report
sources.supports: A peer provincial manager operating on a cost recovery basis: investment management fees are charged to the investment pools and clients; it recovers all of its expenses through the pooled portfolios and segregated client accounts it manages; the primary drivers of investment management costs are assets under management and each client's asset mix; revenue from recoveries of costs equals costs incurred under management contracts; costs split into internal, external direct and external indirect and benchmarked with CEM.

sources.title: Wages: Accountant (NOC 11100) in the Toronto Region
sources.supports: Toronto region hourly wages low $25.00, median $41.34, high $74.36 (reference period 2023-2024).
